forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Mayoral Investment Fund programmes reprioritised with net reduction of £0.443m over MTFP; shift from capital to revenue delivery reflects updated delivery forecasts.
findings.detail: Review of the MIF portfolio concluded additional revenue funding is required for programme delivery while several capital allocations are no longer required at previous levels. MIF Revenue Programme budget increased by £1.182m and Capital Programme reduced by £1.625m in 2026/27. Changes affect Skills Innovation Fund, Active Travel, Town Centres & High Streets and Cost of Living initiatives.
findings.matters: Significant mid-year reprioritisation of delivery approach suggests previous capital intensity assumptions were incorrect, indicating either market changes in how programmes can be delivered or delivery challenges with capital-heavy approaches.
findings.figures: Net reduction £0.443m over MTFP; 2026/27: revenue increase £1.225m, capital decrease £1.837m
findings.quote: The review has concluded that additional revenue funding is required to support programme delivery, whilst several capital allocations are no longer required at the levels previously assumed.

findings.headline: £650k investment approved for Bus Service Delivery Review, a critical programme to transfer bus services control to the Combined Authority from April 2027.
findings.detail: The investment will fund specialist staffing, legal and consultancy support to deliver the transition covering workforce, contractual, financial, legal, ICT and governance arrangements. Funding is available from in-year treasury management income forecast to exceed budget by £1m overall. This represents a new material commitment not included in the original 2026/27 budget.
findings.matters: Material new commitment emerging mid-budget cycle signals either incomplete original planning or changed government requirements. The bus transition is critical to devolution objectives but represents delivery risk requiring significant management resource and signalling programme complexity.
findings.figures: £650k investment required; treasury management income forecast £1m over budget
findings.quote: The Bus Delivery Review is a critical transition programme to prepare the York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority for assuming bus delivery responsibilities from April 2027. The programme covers workforce, contractual, financial, legal, ICT and governance arrangements. A one-off investment of £650k is required to provide resource the project and secure specialist staffing, legal and consultancy support, ensuring the transfer is delivered safely, compliantly and to the required timetable.

findings.headline: Mayoral Capacity Funding: £1.500m budgeting error corrected in June outturn; government confirms allocation of £1.322m (£0.178m below original estimate).
findings.detail: The June outturn report incorrectly reduced the expenditure budget by £1.500m rather than increasing income to reflect anticipated capacity funding. Government has subsequently confirmed the actual allocation at £1.322m, representing a shortfall from the original estimate. This capacity funding is ring-fenced for core capacity investment to support organisation growth and enhanced devolution responsibilities.
findings.matters: Budget correction indicates an internal control issue in how funding allocations were processed. The shortfall from estimated amount affects the Authority's ability to fund core capacity investment. Both matter for credit assessment and governance confidence.
findings.figures: £1.500m error in June budget; £1.322m confirmed allocation versus £1.500m estimate; £0.345m additional staffing overspend in core services
findings.quote: The Budget Outturn Report considered by Cabinet in June 2026 incorrectly reflected an anticipated allocation of £1.500m of additional Mayoral Capacity Funding. In presenting this funding, the expenditure budget was reduced by £1.500m rather than increasing income. Government has since confirmed the additional Mayoral Capacity Funding allocation to be £1.322m, (which is lower than the original estimate of £1.500m).

findings.headline: Brownfield Housing Programme forecast shows £24.159m underspend (17.99% of capital budget) reflecting delivery delays in major schemes.
findings.detail: The underspend is primarily due to claims being linked to start-on-site milestones rather than MHCLG funding timing, and to several major schemes experiencing viability, procurement and planning challenges. The Housing Team is undertaking detailed reforecasting with delivery partners and will bring any consequential budget changes to Cabinet in a separate report. Delivery risks have been escalated to Economy Directorate Management Team with a management action plan in place.
findings.matters: A material underspend in a major housing programme indicates delivery risk or programme overambition. This affects the council's capital deployment efficiency and the pace at which it can deliver housing outcomes — material to lenders and to other councils designing similar programmes.
findings.figures: £24.159m underspend on Brownfield Housing Programme; £25.475m budget against forecast expenditure of £1.317m
findings.quote: The forecast underspend of £24.159m on the Brownfield Housing Programme reflects the rephasing of expenditure into future financial years. This is primarily due to Brownfield Housing Fund claims being linked to start-on-site milestones rather than the timing of MHCLG funding receipts currently reflected in the budget. In addition, several major schemes are experiencing viability, procurement and planning challenges, resulting in delays to anticipated expenditure.

findings.headline: Town Centres programme rebalances £1.1m from capital delivery to revenue funding
findings.detail: Town Centres & High Streets capital funding is reduced by £1,144,385 and revenue funding increased by exactly £1,144,385, indicating a structural shift in programme delivery model.
findings.matters: Large reallocations between capital and revenue for a single programme are unusual and signal delivery model change (infrastructure to grants/revenue support) or timing adjustment; peers track how councils rebalance.
findings.figures: TCHS Capital Budget Change: -£1,144,385. TCHS Revenue Budget Change: +£1,144,385.
